note: Seventeen posts in two batches. Afternoon: a 'News Headlines' cover card with no headlines on it, eight Budget 2027 cards and a Bloomberg world indices screen (08:34 Sri Lanka time). Evening: the daily market snapshot, a sector heat map, three more Budget cards (tourism, railway electrification, levies) and the cover of the broker's 'Budget Review 2027' report, with a shortened link to the full report that was not opened, so its contents are not summarised. No recommendation table or dividend cards were posted, so calls and dividends are empty. Foreign flow figures per stock are read from the snapshot chart's bar labels ('Other', Rs 8mn net bought, is left out); index contributor bars carry no values, so only names are listed. All images were legible.
highlights: A firmer day: the ASPI rose 0.56% (124 points) to 22,157 on a thin Rs 2.98bn turnover, led by Sri Lanka Telecom (up 8.1%), Distilleries, Dialog, Tokyo Cement (up 3.3%) and LOLC Finance.
Foreign investors were net sellers of Rs 111mn, almost all of it Dialog (Rs 153mn sold); they bought Lanka Milk Foods (Rs 23mn) and Packages Lanka (Rs 10mn).

The 2027 Budget dominated the broker's posts. Its review calls it policy continuity with no major tax changes. Infrastructure gets the big numbers: Rs 487bn for road and rail, Rs 80bn to start a Rs 1,200bn+ railway electrification, Rs 50bn for ports and Rs 27.5bn for the grid. That supports contractors and cement makers such as Access Engineering and Tokyo Cement.

Tax changes: personal income tax is cut from 1 April 2027 (tax-free threshold Rs 162,500 a month), the tourism development levy is abolished, import cess is cut 25% on 800 tariff lines, and the levy on imported sugar rises Rs 10 a kg from 13 November.
No new broker ratings or dividend cards today, so there is nothing to set against the site's fair values.

news.title: Market close
news.text: The ASPI gained 124 points (0.56%) and the S&P SL20 0.26% on Rs 2.98bn turnover; the market trades at 11.4 times earnings and 1.31 times book. Sri Lanka Telecom jumped 8.1%, Ceylon Tea Services 5.4%, LOLC Finance 4.1% and Tokyo Cement 3.3%. Foreigners sold Rs 153mn of Dialog, which still closed 0.6% higher.

news.title: Broker's Budget review
news.text: HNB Stockbrokers published a 'Budget Review 2027: Policy Continuity & Fiscal Alignment', saying the budget builds on disciplined fiscal management with no major tax changes, which gives investors more clarity.

news.title: Budget 2027: the big picture
news.text: The President set targets for 2027 of government revenue at 16% of GDP, primary spending at 13.6% of GDP, capital spending at 4.48% of GDP and a primary surplus of 2.3% of GDP. Foreign debt repayments are estimated at about USD 3.0bn in 2027 and USD 3.7bn in 2028.

news.title: Budget 2027: roads and highways
news.text: Rs 487bn goes to building and modernising road and rail, of which Rs 250bn is for expressways and roads. The Ratnapura expressway gets Rs 83bn; the Pothuhera–Galagedara (Rs 23.1bn) and Pothuhera–Rambukkana (Rs 12bn) sections are due to be finished in 2027. A further Rs 8.5bn is set aside for roads connecting to the expressways.

news.title: Budget 2027: ports and airport
news.text: Rs 50bn is allocated to expand port capacity, aiming for more than 30mn containers (TEU) a year by 2040, plus Rs 300mn for another study on the Colombo North Port. The airport's first terminal handles about 9mn passengers a year against a design capacity of 6mn; work on the second terminal is expected to start in 2027.

news.title: Budget 2027: energy and the power grid
news.text: Rs 27.5bn to strengthen the national grid in 2027, a plan for 500MW of floating solar on reservoirs, and Rs 500mn for early work on the Kilinochchi–New Habarana 400kV line (due by 2030, with about USD 150mn expected from the AIIB). Home battery storage gets a subsidy of Rs 25,000 per kW (up to Rs 250,000) and the 10% levy on imported batteries is removed.

news.title: Budget 2027: petroleum
news.text: Fuel storage is to double to 100,000 tonnes, the Sapugaskanda refinery is to be upgraded to 100,000 barrels a day through a public–private partnership, and work has started on a Rs 22.3bn jet fuel storage complex and pipeline from Muthurajawela to the airport.

news.title: Budget 2027: telecoms and digital
news.text: 533 new telecom towers are being built for completion in 2027, with Rs 3.1bn from the telecoms regulator. Spending on digital government and the digital economy rises by Rs 10bn to Rs 28.5bn in total.

news.title: Budget 2027: personal income tax
news.text: From 1 April 2027 the tax-free allowance rises to Rs 1.95mn a year (Rs 162,500 a month). The 6% band shrinks to Rs 850,000, then bands of Rs 600,000 are taxed at 12%, 18%, 24% and 30%, with 36% only above Rs 5.2mn a year. The broker estimates monthly savings of Rs 750 to Rs 15,750 per taxpayer.

news.title: Budget 2027: capital markets
news.text: Rs 500mn, on top of Rs 250mn from the CSE itself, to encourage small and medium companies to list on a dedicated board, and a 'Share for Everyone' programme giving selected Grade 13 students aged 18 and over share portfolios worth up to Rs 10,000.

news.title: World markets overnight
news.text: The morning screen showed most major markets up the previous day: the S&P 500 gained 1.3%, Germany's DAX 1.2% and Korea's KOSPI 1.0%, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 1.2%.

news.title: Budget 2027: railway electrification
news.text: More than Rs 1,200bn is planned to electrify three main lines, starting with Rs 80bn in 2027: Rs 45bn for Maradana–Homagama (Kelani Valley line), Rs 17.7bn for Maradana–Panadura (coastal line), Rs 16.4bn for Maradana–Ragama (main line) and Rs 900mn for land and other costs.

news.title: Budget 2027: levies and import taxes
news.text: The tourism development levy ends on 1 April 2027. Import cess falls 25% on 800 tariff lines, the second step of phased tariff cuts. The 10% ports and airports levy is removed on newsprint and solar storage batteries from 1 January 2027. The special commodity levy is cut on some essential foods but raised Rs 10 a kg on imported sugar from 13 November 2026. Fuel for ships on international voyages is exempted from the social security levy to help bunkering.

news.title: Budget 2027: tourism
news.text: USD 77mn from the World Bank to restore Colombo Fort as a tourism zone, a cruise terminal at Colombo port plus Rs 240mn for terminals at Galle, Tangalle and Trincomalee, a Rs 500mn concessionary loan scheme for tourism equipment such as boats, and Rs 240mn to develop the Dutch forts at Jaffna, Mannar, Kalpitiya and Batticaloa through public–private partnerships.
